caveats: In such cases SparTA enumerates all combinations of block sizes to run the weighted block cover algorithm and pick the best one, which can be expensive.

evidence.support_description: When an operator is too sparse to saturate available cores, the weights may become less accurate; SparTA then enumerates all combinations of block sizes.

findings.claim: Tensor Scrambling is probabilistic and its sample count is empirical, with no formal guarantee that the inferred pruned elements are correct.
findings.mechanism: The rule sets pruned input elements to zero, assigns random values to remaining elements, runs the operator repeatedly, and treats elements that always stay zero as pruned.
caveats: The paper reports that 256 randomly sampled tensors can identify sparsity correctly in their experience, but this is empirical rather than theoretically justified.

evidence.support_description: Tensor Scrambling repeats random sampling; the paper states that 256 randomly sampled tensors can identify sparsity correctly in their experience.

findings.claim: Tensor Scrambling requires at least a dense version of the operator to be available.
findings.mechanism: The probabilistic propagation rule runs the operator on scrambled inputs to observe which output elements always remain zero.
conditions: Dense implementation of the operator available
caveats: If only an opaque or sparse-only operator implementation exists, this propagation rule cannot be applied as described.

evidence.support_description: The rule assumes at least the dense version of the operator is available.

findings.claim: Quantization attribute propagation requires calibration data, fine-tuning, and an accuracy-drop threshold, which may not suit all deployment constraints.
findings.mechanism: SparTA collects calibration data by inference, gradually lowers quantization precision, fine-tunes the operator to minimize MSE, and accepts the new attribute if accuracy drop is below a predefined threshold.
conditions: Train or test dataset available for calibration
caveats: The threshold may not satisfy stricter accuracy requirements.
Calibration data collection and fine-tuning add cost and depend on representative data.

evidence.support_description: The rule uses calibration data, fine-tuning, and accepts lower precision if model accuracy drop is smaller than a predefined threshold such as 1%.

findings.claim: SparTA's performance benefits depend on target hardware support for sparsity and low-bit instructions.
findings.mechanism: Code specialization selects hardware instructions and tiling based on TeSA bit width and block size, such as wmma, DP4A, AVX512 VNNI, or Sparse Tensor Cores.
conditions: Target hardware supports relevant sparsity or quantization instructions
caveats: Benefits may be lower on hardware without such support.
Evaluation covers only specific NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel accelerators.

evidence.support_description: Specialization uses hardware instructions such as wmma, DP4A, AVX512 VNNI, and Sparse Tensor Cores; evaluation is on NVIDIA 2080Ti/A100, AMD Radeon VII, and Intel Xeon Silver 4210.

findings.claim: The evaluation is limited to three DNN models and four representative sparsity patterns, so generality to other models and sparsity schemes is not fully established.
findings.mechanism: SparTA is evaluated on BERT, MobileNet, and HuBERT with structured, unstructured, structured+8bit, and mixed sparsity patterns.
conditions: Patterns: structured, unstructured, structured+8bit, mixed sparsity
Accelerators: CUDA GPU, ROCm GPU, Intel CPU
caveats: Results may not generalize to other model families, sparsity algorithms, or hardware platforms.

evidence.support_description: The evaluation uses three popular DNN models with four representative sparsity patterns on three accelerators.

findings.claim: Sparsity propagation is less effective for unstructured sparsity, especially at moderate sparsity ratios.
findings.mechanism: Propagation rules infer additional pruned elements from operator semantics; unstructured patterns provide fewer regular propagation opportunities than structured patterns.
caveats: Structured sparsity propagation increased total sparsity from 50% to 89.7%, while unstructured sparsity at 90% original sparsity increased only to 95.3%.

evidence.support_description: The propagation ability on unstructured sparsity is lower; only high sparsity ratios bring an obvious increase.

findings.claim: The SparTA implementation is tied to the Rammer compiler and ONNX graph conversion, and portability to other compiler stacks is not evaluated.
findings.mechanism: SparTA is implemented as additional compilation passes over Rammer, and DNN models are converted to ONNX before compiling.
caveats: Porting the approach to other compilers or frameworks may require additional engineering and may not preserve the same performance.

evidence.support_description: SparTA is implemented on Rammer, and a DNN model is converted to an ONNX graph before compiling.

findings.claim: Execution-plan transformation requires profiling on real hardware and iterative search, making compilation hardware-dependent and potentially budget-limited.
findings.mechanism: The transformation policy iterates over transformation options, generates sub-operators, profiles composed graphs on the target hardware, and records performance until a budget or satisfaction condition is met.
caveats: The search budget may prevent finding the best transformation.
Profiling and iterative search increase compile time and require access to the target hardware.

evidence.support_description: TransformOp loops while the policy has budget and performance is not satisfied, profiles composed graphs, and records performance.

findings.claim: The SparTA-based 3DNA training implementation still relies on PyTorch for management of some intermediate tensors, limiting memory optimization.
findings.mechanism: SparTA-based 3DNA is integrated into PyTorch for fair comparison, and PyTorch manages some intermediate tensors.
conditions: Integrated into PyTorch for fair comparison
caveats: The paper states memory usage could be further improved by moving intermediate tensor management to the SparTA side.

evidence.support_description: The SparTA-based version currently relies on PyTorch for management of some intermediate tensors, so memory usage could be further improved.

findings.claim: The termination guarantee for attribute propagation relies on monotonic increase and commutativity/associativity of the current pruning and quantization rules, so new custom rules may not preserve it.
findings.mechanism: Algorithm 1 repeatedly propagates attributes until convergence; the paper argues termination because each propagation monotonically increases sparsity and pruning/quantization propagations are commutative and associative.
conditions: Rules not monotonic, commutative, or associative
caveats: The stated termination guarantee is for the current pruning and quantization propagation rules, not necessarily for arbitrary future rules.

evidence.support_description: The paper states that because each propagation monotonically increases sparsity and both pruning and quantization propagations are commutative and associative, Algorithm 1 is guaranteed to terminate.
